"I intend to help myself to some of your land, fool, and you are powerless to stop me!"
"Your people are unfortunate to be ruled by you. When I take your lands they will finally know greatness!"
"You are a coward and a weakling. Invading you will be a pleasure."
"I am a powerful warrior and you are not. Surrender to me now and maybe I will let you live!"
"This county is vital to my plans. Please relinquish control of it to my lads or face the consequences."
"Sir, this county is part of my ancestral lands and I hereby claim it by right of birth.  Yield or face the might of my army."
"Begone!  You have occupied my lands for far too long. "
"All must fall before the might and right of my cause.  You shall be the first."
"I am intent on restoring my royal banner to this county, that has for so long been without its rightful sovereign."
"The presence of your troops in my lands is most unwelcome.  It is time I removed them!"
"I grow angrier with every second of your insolence.  Shortly this will be fixed when I reclaim my lands!"
"You have governed my lands long enough.  I will take back what is rightfully mine!"
"My troops have entered your county on a purely fact-finding mission, my friend. Please do not be alarmed."
"Out of necessity I have been forced to seize a portion of your realm, Lord. I apologize for the inconvenience."
"By the Church's authority, I hereby seize a portion of your land as my own. Kindly keep your distance."
"The presence of my troops in your county has been deemed necessary by the Church Council. Do not protest--- this action is in everyone's best interests."
"Excellent! I am well pleased with these crowns you have given me. I shall spend them at once."
"Trying to buy the favor of the rich and powerful, are we? Very well, your gift is noted."
"Any coward can send money. Let us see how you fare on the battlefield."
"Your gift has been received. Feel free to send more."
"I thank you for your gift, my Lord, it is most welcome."
"Your tribute is most timely.  I had feared you had forgotten that I am the true heir to the throne."
"This will aid in arming my latest muster. I will keep your generosity in mind after my coronation."
"You are a generous lord, sire. These crowns can only strengthen our growing affinity."
"Maybe I am judging you too harshly. I thank you for your contribution to the cause."
"Your gift is appropriate and does please me. It shall be remembered."
"I have received word of your gift.  It is worthy for someone who shall soon be Queen."
"I perhaps misjudged you.  Your gift causes me to think better of you."
"Many thanks for your most magnanimous donation. You are surely the kindest of all my friends."
"Such a proud gift will surely aid the Church's struggle to bring peace to this troubled land."
"Your gift reveals a fine and honorable character, my son. Rest assured that it will be put to good use."
"Your benevolence knows no bounds, good man. You and I shall get along splendidly."
"Thanks for the gold, but it is not very much, is it? Can you send more next time?"
"This gift is barely acceptable. I assume there is more on the way."
"I suppose I must thank you for the crowns. But really, I deserve more than this."
"You gift is so modest, it barely merits a reply."
"This tribute proves that you are a loyal vassal.  Maybe you should delve deeper into your treasury for your next payments."
"The war has escalated, sir, and so have my expenses.  As a loyal vassal I would expect you to consider this before sending next year's tithe."
"I accept your meager gift, but I must remind you that such paltry sums do little justice to your honor."
"Your tribute is most welcome.  However, I am sure that in your haste to dispatch this gift, you forgot to include the rest of it."
"I appreciate your desire to gain favor at our court. But please do not think we will be fooled so easily by your paltry gift of crowns."
"Your gift is generous for someone of your means.  It is, however, not enough to buy my favor."
"You should be pleased to know your gift was well received by the peasants.  Send word when I can expect mine."
"I regret to inform you that your gift is of little use for someone like myself.  I look forward to seeing your next one."
"Well, I suppose 'tis the thought that counts... The Church thanks you for your gift, meager though it was."
"Your small token has been received. Between you and me, if you want to make an impression, you will have to send more next time."
"I had hoped for more from a ruler as wise and prosperous as you. Oh well, I guess I was expecting too much."
"Some of my lowest advisors have donated more gold than you. I guess you are not as strong as I thought, and I had such high hopes for you..."
"Methinks you have forgotten that you curry favor with a noble.  Such paltry sums insult me."
"So little gold!  Can you not match even your own meager standards?"
"Your gift is too small. You must send more if you want to buy my friendship."
"I've received many gifts from nobles like you wanting to buy my favor. Yours is among the lowest. Do better next time."
"My noble friend, please guard your gold shipments more carefully. By the time your envoy arrived he was only carrying a few small coins."
"You're latest 'tribute' payment was an intolerable jest.  Can you really believe I will be impressed with such ridiculous gestures ?"
"The stable boy appreciated your amusing gift. Now, where is mine ?"
"We appreciate the sentiment in your latest tithe - but, lord, this must be a mistake. There are but a few crowns here."
"You must think me very stupid indeed, if you think such a trifling amount of money can buy you favor at our court. Please do not insult my intelligence again."
"Any gift that makes it through your territories unmolested must surely be of trivial importance. As I have just learned myself. "
"What was your intention with that gift?  If it was to insult me, you were successful."
"Your gift was received and it now has a prominent position worthy of its value.  The only problem is, our pigs keep trying to feed upon it."
"Oh dear, that really was a pittance, wasn't it? The Church cannot survive on such sums, my lord."
"My good fellow, surely the trifling sum I have received from your realm was not intended as a gift. Perhaps some of it was lost on the way?"
"Surely so great a noble as yourself can afford more than that, my Lord. The Church's needs are great."
"Ah, such a modest gift from abroad. Have you fallen on hard times, lad?"
"What can I say? Greatness runs in the family."
"Your compliment has reached me. My opinion of you has risen... slightly."
"I see that word of my greatness has reached your ears. Thank you for the compliment."
"Thank you for your compliment. Let me tell you more about myself... I am the strongest man I have ever seen!"
"You think far too highly of me, my noble friend.  Methinks your flowery words reach too many ears."
"Despite my better judgment, I find myself swayed by the honor of your words."
"Your kind letter was most timely, sir.  Your silence was bordering on insult.  You are wise to show your respect in such a manner. "
"If we had a man of mettle on the throne, I would be glad to idly chat the days away. But in dire times, action is needed."
"You pay me my just respect, and that pleases me. I shall remember your courtesy. "
"It is good to hear such kind words from you.  We should exchange letters more often."
"Your words are most kind.  I was unaware that you are capable of such prose."
"I am pleased by your words and have spread the word throughout my court."
"Your love for the Church is well known, my child. I am sure your faith will be repaid in coming times."
"Your kind words are as well-said as they are true. Stick with me and you shall go far!"
"Why, thank you for the compliment, good fellow. You are a fine judge of character."
"The Church thanks you for your kind message. You are most insightful."
"Yes, I heard you the first time. You think I am great, I know. When I have need for you, I will let you know."
"Yet another compliment from beyond the hills.  Perhaps you should kneel before me as your superior."
"I am sure you stand in awe of my skills. Watch me and you may learn something, fellow."
"Yes, I know you think I am fantastic. You have already told me, and I still agree with you."
"I have read your second letter, my lord, and am pleased. However, events are overtaking us and it is action that is needed now, not words."
"These soft words warm my heart but do not feed my men.  If you are truly my friend send proof of your sincerity."
"Faint praise, sir, is as valuable as a feather in the wind.  I accept your compliment ... but where is your tribute?  Gold would add weight to your words."
"Your latest letter is as fair as your first. But these words do not move the crown one inch closer to my head."
"You grace us with further honorable words. Your loyalty has now been firmly impressed upon us."
"Twice you have now made your favor towards me known.  Twice I have been very happy with your words."
"Your continued praise of my empire is very commendable.  I will keep it in mind."
"It pleases me greatly to see you pay me the respect I deserve.  I give you my thanks."
"Another compliment, my lord! Why, we are favored. I must thank you again."
"You flatter me, kind sir. If you can rule as skillfully as you speak, you are surely bound for greatness!"
"Your compliments are a fine tribute, my lord. The Church Council looks fondly upon you."
"Your faith in the Church is well-placed, child. You may trust me, but be wary of all others. "
"You are boring me now with your groveling letters. Do not send me any more."
"I am quite tired of your compliments. Perhaps if I have your hands cut off, you will be able to write no more."
"Your fondness for  me far surpasses the bounds of decency. Keep your bootlicking to yourself and bother me no more."
"Stop your groveling immediately. I have no need for compliments from foolish upstarts like you."
"You are too free with your compliments. I have no more breath to waste on trivial pleasantries and am distressed to find that you do."
"I tire of your constant flattery and flowery prose.  Without action or tribute your words ring false."
"You must be wearing out your horses, sending these verses so often. Would that they carried Knights to fight our enemies or gold to the rightful King!"
"Mere words, my friend, will not stop the usurpers. Only men, blood, and steel will aid my cause."
"I am starting to suspect your motives behind this campaign of flattery. You would do well not to underestimate my intelligence."
"Your flattery is welcomed, but I am unsure what it is you want.  Be more direct next time. You have proved worthy of it."
"Although I deserve all the respect and flattery you have shown me, I have a feeling that something more lies behind these exchanges."
"True enough that I am all as you say.  However, there is no more you can say without me getting suspicious of your motives."
"I know your admiration for me is great, as it should be. But try to contain yourself."
"Your words carry less authority with each repetition.  Speak through your actions, if you would be believed henceforth."
"The Church has no shortage of words, my lord.  Pray send me no more."
"You have shown us your skill with the pen, my Lord. Channel your energies elsewhere, for when the storm breaks, mere words will provide no shelter."
"You must learn respect for your superiors.  I relish the day when I cut your tongue from your head."
"How dare you insult me from afar!  You shall pay for your insolence, you rat!"
"You are ugly and stupid, and you smell bad. Everyone thinks so."
"Insult me? That is a mistake! I remember the last fellow who did such a thing. His head is mounted on my wall."
"Your insults are hurtful, my friend - but they hurt less than my steel, I would wager!"
"We have long been rivals, but your unjust words will make us enemies.  Cease your evil slandering or I will stop at nothing to destroy you."
"You stand, like a sniveling child, hurling words where your deeds dare not tread."
"Do I hear the crowing of a strutting cock? I must send for the butcher, to end its infernal racket."
"Your disrespect astonishes us.  You have disgraced your name forever in these halls."
"You loathsome worm!  You shall pay for your disrespect!"
"Insult me?  How dare you!  This will not easily be forgotten."
"Vile pig!  I will not stand for insults from such common vermin."
"You are misguided, my child. There is little to be gained from your rude and childish remarks."
"How dare you hurl such rubbish at me from afar! Speak such filth to me in person and I shall have my henchmen deal with you directly! "
"You have all the grace and good looks of a pond leech, and your foul-smelling county is an embarrassment to the nation."
"Really sir, if you think that such crude and lowly language befits a noble, then I pity you."
"You, help me? You must be joking. Go away. "
"I do not need any help from you. Go away."
"An alliance? You just want to ride my coattails to the throne. The answer is no."
"I got a hearty laugh out of your last message. Why would a great noble like me want an alliance with a nobody like you?"
"I have studied your offer well, but I see no sense in us joining together at the present time."
"I seek not casual friendships with underlings.  Acknowledge my rightful claim through regular tribute.  When you have proven the honor of your words I will reconsider your offer."
"Although your heart is strong, your arm falters under the weight of responsibility. An alliance will not further my cause at this time."
"A drowning man will clutch at anything. I fear you would hinder the cause more than strengthen it."
"I do not think it would be fitting for our two houses to join as one. You are forgetting who I am, my lord."
"The time is not right for us to ally.  I choose to decline your offer."
"Your proposal has been carefully considered.  Perhaps some time later."
"I welcome your offer, but there really is no need for us to ally now."
"Unfortunately, and with great sadness, I must decline your offer of a treaty, my noble lord."
"Though I would truly welcome an alliance with your grace, sir, I must decline. The Almighty has advised me otherwise."
"The Church has carefully considered your reputation and has decided to decline your offer. Perhaps you should find a less respectable kingdom, and offer your services there."
"Your offer is noted, good sir, but I am doing just fine without your help. The answer is no."
"Yes, I will let you fight with me - but no tricks, and do not forget that I am in charge."
"As an act of charity to you, I accept your offer of an alliance. I hope you appreciate my generosity."
"I am not sure I trust you, but all right. I accept your offer. Do not disappoint me."
"Oh yes, I would like to be your ally. Who shall we destroy first?"
"Your counsel is good. We will fight together and we shall win together."
"Your offer is wise and honorable.  I accept.  All must fall before the might of our forces."
"The earth will shake when our men-at-arms join in battle. Let the curs run and hide from the light of our righteousness. I accept."
"The scribes will write volumes of the deeds we two shall accomplish. I heartily accept an alliance with your lordship."
"We accept your request to fight under our banner."
"It gladdens me to see your offer of alliance.  I accept."
"Your proposed alliance is acceptable to me.  We shall fight together!"
"I am satisfied that your intentions are good.  Your offer is accepted."
"An alliance, what a splendid idea! In these troubled times, the Church needs great allies such as yourself."
"My skill and holy favor, combined with your land and money?... Ah yes!  May our great alliance trumpet a new age of peace and prosperity!"
"I will agree to form an alliance with you, my good sir, but I will hold you to your vow. Should you betray me, your downfall will be swift!"
"I most graciously accept your offer, good sir. The Church is your ally."
"Look, I am in a generous mood, so I hereby offer you an alliance. You would be wise to accept it."
"You are almost as skilled on the battlefield as I. Why do we not take up arms together, and brutalize our common foes?"
"In these uncertain times, leaders like you might have troubles. I offer you an alliance."
"Look, I do not want to, but I am going to offer you an alliance. Take it, or leave it?"
"I offer you an alliance my lord. I have thought long over this, and at present, both our interests would be better served if we were to fight as one."
"Our paths are as one, my Lord, as are our enemies.  An alliance would help us both. Will you accept ?"
"You are deemed worthy of an alliance with our cause. Shall we together set right the wrongs of our enemies ?"
"In battle, you set both hands upon your hilt, so as to strike down your foe. Will you be my right hand and help end the strife with one swift blow ?"
"Our two noble houses should not quarrel my lord. Can we not, instead, come to some mutual understanding?"
"I ask you to fight alongside me.  Help me achieve my right and you shall be rewarded."
"You have proved yourself worthy of my trust.  I ask you to join me in alliance."
"This kingdom needs strong lords.  Aid me and I shall make you the strongest of them all."
"We need not be enemies, my child. Why not sign this treaty I have prepared and let our interests join, that we should both be the stronger for it."
"My son, you rule your people with strength and honor. Why not bind your fate with that of the Church?  An alliance could strengthen you and me alike."
"There is treachery afoot, my son. Swear an alliance with me, and we shall form a power to be reckoned with!"
"Your noble lands abound in wealth, my friend. You are clearly a great leader. An alliance between you and me would be a great honor."
"Well, our alliance has been fun, but I have grown bored with it. It is over. Good bye."
"My realm is growing more powerful by the minute. I no longer need your help. Our alliance is broken."
"Your attitude annoys me. Consider our alliance broken."
"I know I agreed to be your ally, but you have been nothing but a bother. Our alliance is over."
"The time has come, my friend, for us to part company. Our union has served us well over the years, but now the real contest begins."
"Our alliance has been increasingly burdensome.  No longer do I see enough value in maintaining it to counterbalance its cost.  Our alliance is hereby terminated."
"It is best to crush the adder under foot, before it strikes. And I have seen you coiling for some time. Our alliance is finished."
"You have been most chivalrous in your agreement with me, my lord. But now, I fear, unless you are prepared to kneel before me, we must meet in battle."
"There is no longer a need for us to be bound by treaty.  We shall go our own ways."
"Our paths must now diverge.  Perhaps we shall join forces at a later time."
"Your services are no longer required.  If I need them again, I shall send word."
"The Church feels that you are strong enough now to move out from under its protective wing and fight your own battles!"
"Alas, my lord, the Church has no further need of your assistance. Our alliance is broken. Go as you would, but do not cross my path."
"I'm afraid that forces greater than you and I have requested that our alliance be broken. With apologies to you, I must comply."
"Political tides have shifted since we sealed our pact. Regrettably, the Church's interests are better served by severing our friendship. I warn you to stay clear of my borders."
"You are lower than a weasel's backside. You have broken our alliance, and you shall be punished."
"Ha! You may walk out on me now, but you will come crawling back when I am King. You wait and see."
"Ah, you have broken your word. I expected as much. You have only harmed yourself, foolish sir."
"You are a liar! Do you know what I do to liars? I cut them in two. I am sharpening my sword right now, so watch yourself."
"You damned fool! If you wish for a fight, then so be it."
"I have maintained our alliance in good faith, sir, but your treachery has not gone unnoticed. We are enemies once more. Beware."
"Perfidious scoundrel!  I accepted you as an honorable ally and this is my reward?  Make peace with your maker for your days are numbered!"
"Your scandalous actions have only one answer: the headman's ax. You will rue the day you betrayed me."
"You are a coward and a knave, my lord. I hereby strip you of all honors, and if you dare to show your face again, I shall have you hung, drawn and quartered."
"You have violated our agreement.  No longer are we allies."
"Treachery will not be tolerated!  If I set eyes upon you again it will be your last day."
"Your actions have left me little choice but to end our treaty.  Pray I do nothing worse."
"Ohhhhh... fiddle, I knew I should never have trusted you. You are a great disappointment, my child."
"You thieving rogue! How dare you break your promise to the Church!?  You will pay dearly for this outrage!"
"Good sir, you have broken a sacred oath to a peaceful ally. You are a liar and a miscreant. Be assured: your betrayal shall not go unpunished."
"What...? How dare you go behind my back! I will get you for this! I will punish you! Curse you and all the dim-witted minions you command!"
"As soon as trouble breaks you come to me eh? Well, my answer is no, fish face. Fight your own battles."
"I  take orders from no man. Fight your own battles if you are so great. I cannot be bothered."
"My troops cannot be bothered with your trifles. Handle it yourself."
"You ask me to put my own men on the line for you? You must be crazy. You will be finished soon, anyway."
"I am sorry, my lord, but I am far too weak myself at the moment to come to your assistance."
"Regrettably, I myself am also hard-pressed.  I cannot provide assistance with my own lands so insecure."
"Alas, my troops are far afield and I am unable to relieve you in your hour of need."
"There comes a time in life when you must stand alone. Be brave and strong."
"We have other matters on our mind at the present. Helping you out is out of the question, I fear."
"As the rightful ruler of these lands, my forces have much to do.  I am afraid that I have no spare forces at this time."
"I wish I could lend aid to you now.  However, I have too many other pressing issues at hand."
"At this point in time I must regretfully decline your request for help.  I assure you it is nothing personal."
"It is with a tear in my eye that I must inform you that matters outside of my control will prevent me from coming to your assistance."
"I would dearly love to do as you request, but I fear that my legions are not quite up to the task as yet. Terribly sorry, perhaps next time."
"Hmmmm... you have my utmost sympathy, but I fear that I cannot offer the assistance you desire. 'Tis my busy season, you see..."

"I regret that I cannot send the assistance you request. My troops are currently undergoing an exercise regimen, and thus will be unavailable for quite some time. I do look forward to your next crisis, though. Surely I shall help you then..."
"Of course, I will help you. My soldiers are the best in the land, and  I welcome the chance to prove it once again."
"Certainly, I shall help you.  I am good at fighting, even if you are not."
"You are lucky to have allied yourself with me. I shall grant your request, but you remember this!"
"Ah, good. I have just purchased a new flail, and am eager to try it out. To battle!"
"I am, this very day, marshaling a company of troops to come to your assistance."
"Of course, my lord.  My sworn allegiance was not false.  May these hardy men I am sending restore peace in your lands."
"I have mustered my commoners, and they are sent to you with godspeed."
"To horse! To horse! We are called once again to aid our brethren."
"Our alliance holds true. I will help you in your hour of need."
"As the rightful Queen, I honor all requests from my loyal Lords.  Aid will come forthwith."
"We have many pressing needs, but I will make sure you get the help you need."
"I will do whatever is necessary to help you in your hour of need."
"Fear not, my trusted ally. I shall dispatch some of my men immediately."
"Honored ally, if trouble threatens, I will gladly risk the lives of others to heed your call for help! Your request will be granted!"
"I suppose I could spare some of my troops to come to your aid. In the future, please try to settle your affairs on your own accord."
"I shall send you the aid you request. Consider yourself indebted."
"I cannot go running off every time you ask for help. To get my help, you must send gold."
"I would be happy to help you in your time of need, but you must prove yourself worthy. Please send money - that will do the trick."
"If you want my help, you will have to send gold, moneybags. I cannot do everything."
"Do you think that gold grows on trees, fellow? Send money, and perhaps I will help you as you request."
"I would be happy to send a force to relieve you, if only I had the crowns to pay the wages of my men.  If you would be so kind..."
"Many would willingly fight for me but my coffers are empty.  If you could provide the money for their equipment and pay I would gladly raise an army to assist you."
"Alas, I have not the funds to come to your aid. If you would pay for the muster, I have the men for you."
"The glint of gold would summon the eyes of my fighting men. Send forth a warchest."
"The royal coffers are low at the moment. We will need some financial help from you, if we are to move."
"Our alliance holds true, but we are short on gold at the moment.  You will need to provide for the soldiers' pay.  "
"Since our soldiers will not die for another without pay, we need to receive gold for their services."
"Our alliance is important to me, but so too are the resources of my land.  Send compensation and help will be gladly sent."
"The Church elders are hesitant about coming to your aid. I feel a small donation for the poor might just help focus their minds."
"You ask a great favor, my son. Perhaps if you would send a small token of appreciation for our trouble...?"
"It seems that you are in a bit of a quandary... I will send help - if you are willing to pay for it."
"Alas. My scribes inform me that we cannot spare the funds to fulfill your request. A donation from you might just do the trick."
"I have my own troubles without coming to your rescue all the time. Solve your problems yourself!"
"No, no, no, sorry. My men have been fighting too long, and they need rest."
"Sorry, we have a big jousting tournament to prepare for, and we are busy practicing. Maybe next time."
"Would you have me fight all your battles? No, this one is your problem, not mine."
"There is dirty work afoot, and I will not be part of it. Attack them yourself, my ally."
"I am not your pawn to be ordered into slaughter.  If you want something done, do it yourself."
"Do you seek to bewitch me with words so that I will perform your villainous deeds ? Begone."
"It is time for you to be a man and face the consequences of your deeds alone."
"An excellent target for our troops, my lord. But it should be you that has the honor of crushing our enemies."
"My Lord, even you cannot need my help for this trifling battle."
"They are a motley group. I am sure that you can dispatch them without my aid."
"I would attack if the time were right for me.  Currently, the time is not good."
"Oh no, no ,no, we could not possibly. This would be far too uncharitable an act for the Church to countenance."
"Oh dear, I fear the Church will have to take the path of peace on this matter.  We cannot help you now".
"The Council has carefully considered your request. What you ask holds no benefit for us. We must refuse."
"An attack, now? Oh my no, the time is not right for such a thing."
"Finally, some action. By all means, yes! I shall attack."
"Oh good, I am getting bored with all this talk. 'Tis time for some bloodshed!"
"My sword is sharp and my armor is shined. You can count on me, ally."
"I did not pledge my alliance for nothing, you know. If you need something done, I am your man."
"Now you are talking! I have been waiting for some decisive action from you. We are finally moving towards our goal."
"Long have I awaited the moment to claim those lands.  Your timing is exquisite. I will not fail."
"That braying ass has had it coming for a long time, and I want to be there to watch his head bounce off the turf."
"The time for words is passed. Men of action are needed. I will be there."
"The royal standard is prepared. On the morrow we will march to war. It is time that I am rid of this irritation in any case."
"I shall attack.  Soon my armies will make their presence known to our enemies."
"I confide in you that I have been planning such an attack.  The time draws near."
"Your request for aid is granted.  My knights are preparing for the attack as we speak!"
"My men are ready and I sense victory, my lord. Right will overcome."
"The time for battle is upon us, my friend! With God's blessing, my men shall triumph!"
"Your tactics are cunning indeed, my lord. We shall do as you say."
"The deed you suggest is insidious and underhanded. Noble -- I admire that! Your request will be granted."
"I am not doing this for free. I have weapons to buy, you know. So cough up if you want my help."
"My expert services do not come cheap. Send me some gold, and I will do as you ask."
"An invasion? I would do it just for fun, but for some reason my generals want to be paid. You will need to send some coin this time."
"You have come to the right person. Send me some gold, and you shall see who is truly great in a fight!"
"I will attack. But, by thunder, I SHALL want paying well for this bloody work."
"I am eager for action, but my army will not fight without pay.  If you would finance this endeavor I could set forth immediately."
"I am dangerously short of the weapons of war. If you supply the crowns, I will do this deed."
"I need crowns to maintain my troops in the field. Send gold if you wish my aid. "
"The royal coffers are getting extremely low.  Pay us and we will fight."
"I agree that something needs to be done.  But action is costly."
"I do not help those who do not help me in return. Send gold and I will act."
"I shall take care of this problem for you.  However, you must make it worth my while."
"The Church elders do worry about all this aggression. A little gift may soothe their consciences."
"My generals are ready, but lack a proper motivation in this matter. A gift might help to demonstrate your devotion to the cause."
"Such favors require more than mere gratitude, lord. We shall do as you wish, but for a price."
"Oh my, no, we could never do that.... Unless, of course, some compensation were offered in return."
"I am going to take this here mace, and WHAM! make blood pudding from your brains. So, go away. "
"Look, normally I would have killed you by now, but I like you, so here is a warning: stop it or I shall chop your arms and legs off."
"Nobody is stupid enough to violate my borders. I assume your recent actions have been an accident, and I will let you off with a warning this time."
"Please continue to violate my borders. Then I shall finally have an excuse to run you through, you warthog."
"You are becoming a problem, my friend. If you do not desist in your current aggressive stance, you will leave me no choice but to attack."
"Your recent actions have threatened our friendship.  Desist at once.  I do not desire a war with you, but neither would I shrink from one."
"You tread a fine line. One which I guard with a terrible vengeance. Consider yourself warned."
"It takes a brave man, or a fool, to bait a bear. You, sir, are looking more the fool."
"What is the meaning of your continued aggression towards us? Cease your attacks immediately."
"You must learn that it is I who shall rule this land."
"Why do you insist on interfering with my divine right to rule?"
"You are beginning to anger me.  Continue like this and you shall barely live long enough to regret it."
"Your continual disrespect for the Church's lands is becoming most tiresome, my lord. We advise you take a softer line with us."
"Your insolent behavior is beginning to anger the Church Council. We demand that you show proper respect for our lands."
"I warn you, noble -- the Church will not sit still for such transgressions.  Mend your ways!"
"We wish for no strife with you, lord. We are willing to overlook your recent offense - this time."
"I have had just about enough of you. One more, just one more attack - and that is it. You will get yours."
"You cannot be as big a fool as your actions would have me believe.  I will excuse your foolish ways this last time."
"Listen, you little twit. Keep it up and you are going to get it."
"If you keep attacking me I shall send a small portion of my army to come and pulverize you."
"Your provocations are intolerable.  Withdraw and make amends, or face my wrath".
"Enough of your childish behavior. Your actions carry grave penalties. Desist."
"You caper about like a fool full of too much wine. Stop, and think of your actions, before it is too late."
"You are standing at the abyss. And I am close behind. Shall it be a helping hand, or a mailed fist?"
"I am today advising my captains that any more incursions made under your banner will irrevocably place us at war."
"You are a source of irritation that I shall not long ignore!"
"If you value your time on Earth, pay me my right of respect!"
"Your insolence can be tolerated only so long.  You are fast approaching that time."
"You are intolerable, my lord. Your troops make bloody war in our lands, and you yourself show little regard for our status. We are considering action."
"I shall not stand still for your blatant encroachments upon our peaceful realm. You must cease this recklessness at once, or we shall teach you a lesson you shan't easily forget!"
"You must stop this at once! I will not stand for such defiance! Mend your ways at once, or I shall be forced to take action!"
"Good sir, your rash offenses are unfortunate. The Church has powers you know not. Do not test us!"
"Oh, now you have done it. You have crossed me for the last time. I shall have your head."
"An enormous army is amassing beneath my window right now. I cannot be held responsible for what I do to you when I find you."
"Severed limbs, gaping wounds, crushed heads, burning flesh ...These are a few of my favorite things."
"Be afraid, be very afraid. I am coming to get you, and I never lose."
"I have warned you many times not to interfere with my affairs, but you would not listen. So be it. Now you will pay the price."
"Ungrateful wretch!  Will you stop at nothing?  I will tolerate you no longer: prepare to die."
"I have selected a very special pike. It is the one upon which your head will soon be stuck."
"I will hunt you to the ends of the Earth. I will give no quarter. You have signed your death warrant."
"It is war, then. That is what you seem to want of me, and I will take pleasure in giving it to you."
"You shall no longer soil my lands with your filth!  Your end draws near, wretch."
"Thy days are numbered.  You will soon pay for your sins with your head!"
"There is little left for you to do but pray that you die quickly!"
"The time for talk is over. We shall make an example of you and your tyranny."
"I'll have you know, you rogue, that my armies are strong and well-armed. I am almost certain they will beat you."
"Your vile conduct has surpassed every attempt to deal with you in good faith. You will now answer to my armies!"
"If force is the only authority you answer to, then so be it! My armies have been ordered to show no mercy."
"Why, you are doing miserably! And I thought you were smart ... I must be the only one around here who knows how to run a kingdom."
"Take my advice, friend: step down at once. You will never be King. You are not smart enough or strong enough, like me."
"Ha ha, I knew you would fail miserably, and that is just what it looks like you are doing. Do not say I did not warn you fairly."
"Since you are doing so poorly, here is some friendly advice: give all your land to me. When I have things running smoothly, maybe I will put you in charge again."
"Well, my friend, you have gotten yourself into a fine mess here.  If you wish your people well, surrender and allow me to rule them."
"Be mindful of your lands, sir.  Only a strong economy can produce and support strong armies."
"In order to rule as King, one must have subjects. I advise you to start small and keep your wet nurse handy."
"How any man could turn such a lush county into a vast wasteland, in such a short time, is beyond me."
"You are fighting a lost cause now, my lord. You will never take my rightful place as ruler of these lands. Yield to me now and I may be merciful."
"Why do you not end your quest for the throne before I end your miserable life?"
"There might be a use for you when I rule all these lands.  I could use another pig farmer!"
"Why question and challenge destiny?  I shall rule, and you shall not.  Yield now!"
"Oh dear, Oh dear, how the mighty are humbled. You have cared for your people badly, my lord, and now, it seems, your sins are catching up with you!"
"Tsk, tsk, tsk... my goodness, but you are in a fix. Perhaps you should surrender to me now - your rebellious peasantry just might forgive your inadequacies before they have your head on a stake."
"Neighbor, my scouts report trouble in your lands. You must keep your peasants happy, for they are a rebellious lot!"
"My Lord, your reputation suffers. Perhaps you should reconsider your current course of action."
"Well, everyone knew it would happen... My rule is growing stronger by the minute. Soon I will be King - How fine I shall look in my new crown."
"My realm is far, far better than yours, neighbor. Allow me to rub your nose in it."
"Because I am such a great leader, I am planning a huge festival in my honor. You are not invited."
"Perhaps when I am King I will let you shine my boots. Perhaps you would be good at that!"
"The kingdom is within my grasp, it seems. Only a catastrophe can stop me now."
"The Kingdom will inevitably fall under my rule, as is my right.  Surrender now or perish with the others."
"I have seen rabid sheepdogs tend to their flocks better than you manage your lands. Would you not be happier under my rule?"
"Ha! The Vikings had better land management skills than you."
"My destiny is fast approaching. Then this kingdom shall once again be united under its true and proper Queen."
"I see that your time on this Earth is limited.  A shame, the world needs jesters!"
"Very soon you shall see my destiny fulfilled in all its glory.  Your fate will not be as pleasant."
"As my power grows, I fear that soon we shall never speak again.  One can not speak without a head."
"The power of the Church is growing fast. Events move on apace, and soon, methinks, a new power will hold these lands firmly in its grasp."
"I trust you have heard of the Church's fast-growing power throughout the lands. Providence, it seems, is with me. The Bishop's influence has outpaced your frail reign, my unfortunate foe. "
"Your effort has been noble, my child. But my realm is the most powerful in the land. Soon all will kneel before me! "
"Neighbor, you toil in vain while my Greatness grows. Your struggle is hopeless, and I soon will wear the crown."
"I cannot believe my run of bad luck... How can I have lost?! It is not fair and it is not right."
"You  may think me beaten, but I am not. I still have my sword. I shall take you and your whole army myself with my... wait, my sword.. where is it?... AAAH!"
"What, you have beaten me? You must have cheated! Some day I shall be back. You watch yourself ... some day..."
"Oh no, no, no, I am ruined. I did everything right... My advisors failed me. My generals failed me. 'Tis all their fault..."
"I am ruined, my noble friend. But I am not bitter. I shall return."
"Evil reigns supreme while justice and honor are cast out.  The world is upside down.  This is a dark day for our noble land."
"Alas, my fair land is to fall beneath the shod boots of these curs. Have pity on them, they are just common folk."
"Treachery and villainy have caused the righteous King to fall to such depths. A pox on you all."
"I pity these poor shires, that are not to have their Queen.  Your idiocy will surely ruin all that was once rich!"
"For now you may have bested my forces, but you can not change my right to rule!"
"I fear for your fate on your judgment day.  You have interfered with my divine right to rule."
"Your rule shall not last.  Your incompetence will soon bring you to a ghastly end!"
"No this can't be. Where are my brave men, my troops...... Please show mercy my lords.. please..I beg you.. let me live...."
"Arrrrrghhh! My realm is lost... my power... my crown... my riches... for shame, for shame. Surely, lord, there is a job for me in your new kingdom?"
"Oohhh, I have tried to deal nobly with you, my lord, but your underhanded corruption has beaten me. Your wickedness will not escape judgment."
"I am beaten for now, you fiend. But do not count me out... I'll be back... you'll see! You will live to regret what you have done to me!"
"At last, I am King. What a glorious day! At last all is mine. Soon I will rule the world!"
"I have beaten you, my enemy. There is no honor in defeat. I suggest you go and crawl into a hole somewhere and hide."
"I have won! I have really won! I cannot believe - I mean, of course I have won. I never had any doubts."
"I am King, and you are not. That must feel terrible. Too bad."
"You fools, I was always the one. If only you had listened to me from the beginning all this bloodshed and misery could have been avoided."
"Right has prevailed, as it always will.  If you had submitted at once I would have pardoned you, but the blood shed in this trial by arms cannot be forgiven."
"Does the prisoner have anything to say before the execution? I thought not. May the Lord have mercy on your soul, for you will get none from me."
"Sir, there is a pike waiting outside for your head. Are you ready to part with it?"
"My rightful position is restored. Once more these lands are united - and may they stay ever so!"
"Now that my rule is as it should be, the kingdom is at last at peace!"
"Your fate was sealed the day you crossed me.  Now I shall take my rightful place as Queen!"
"Your pathetic attempt to thwart justice is now at an end. I may be merciful toward you. Then again I may not."
"The Church has been vindicated in its crusade to wipe out tyranny from these shires. Now I shall take the crown and all shall kneel before me."
"You and your evil ways have been defeated. I am victorious! The lands are mine to rule as I please. Long Live the King!"
"The crown is mine, noble foe. As I told you, your silly campaign was but a folly. Now, kneel before my feet and proclaim my greatness for all to hear! HA HA HA !"
"Ha! The throne is mine, and you are defeated at last! Expect no pardon from me, sir. Now, you shall suffer for your contempt!"
"You must be joking. I will never trust you again, ever."
"Oh, do not make me laugh! I need no alliance with you. You are not important at all."
"I heard that you are a liar and a thief. I have enough of that kind of thing already, go away."
"You are a kind and peace-loving leader. I have my reputation to think of!... I will deal with you no more."
"After your complete lack of honor in your last treaty. I had thought to credit you with more intelligence than to ask me again."
"Your treachery makes you more dangerous as an ally than an enemy.  Do not mistake me for a fool."
"Sorry, whelp. I have found real men to aid my cause."
"I suppose we need someone to polish my armor. Can you handle the job? I think not."
"I am sorry, my lord, I could not possibly ally with the likes of you.  What would my people think? "
"In a short while you will not even live.  Why would I wish to ally with you?"
"Your offer is somewhat puzzling to me.  After all, we have nothing pleasant to say to each other."
"If I allied with filth like you, I would not be fit to rule this realm."
"We have been deeply saddened by your treachery of recent times. We will deal with you no more."
"The Church does not wish to be aligned with the likes of you and your roving brigands. Bother me no more with your silly offers."
"Sorry, no. The Church has no need for an alliance with you. Prove your worth, and perhaps we shall reconsider."
"An alliance with you? Oh my, no. You are but a feeble upstart, and you offer nothing to the great and powerful Church. "
"No, I have already got an alliance right now."
"My ally and I are currently plotting your destruction.  Maybe I will ally with you later ... if you are still alive."
"Why would I want to ally with a weakling like you, when I already have an alliance?"
"I already have an ally.  I do not need another one."
"I am sorry my friend, but I am already committed elsewhere."
"I thank you for your kind offer, but I have sworn allegiance to another.  I hope this refusal does not prevent us from continuing our friendship."
"I have no more time for your endless words. I have allies who are men of mettle. May you die well."
"The future King waits for no man. I have found others to pay me homage."
"We will not ally with you. We have other, more trusted, lords who we could not possibly disappoint."
"I have considered your offer, but I presently have other interests."
"If I need another ally, I will be sure to send word.  Until then, I do not."
"There is nothing that can be gained by an alliance between us.  I decline your offer."
"The Church has already made many good friends. We do not presently seek any more, my lord"
"Your request comes too late, my lord. We are already well allied with forces other than yours, and have no need for your friendship."
"The Church declines your request, neighbor. Take my advice: there are forces at work in the land that you cannot possibly challenge. Give up quietly."
"I must decline your offer of friendship, sir. You have nothing to offer me."
Feed your peasants to keep them happy and make them multiply.
Make weapons and create an army.
Right click on items for information.  Left click to perform actions.
Use the slider bar to divide peasants between farming and industry (forestry, iron mining, stone quarrying and weapon making).
Clicking on industries on the map switches them on and off.
Changes you make in a county do not take place until the following season.
Cattle provide dairy foods each season, or they can be eaten.
Wheat can be bought from a merchant and planted in winter. Click on a fallow field to change its usage.
Plan ahead several seasons. Don't get caught without food for your peasants.
High taxes and army recruiting lower happiness.
Very low happiness could result in riots.
Click on a county to go to that county
Click on any area for details about it.
Click and drag a box around any peasants you wish to move, then click on the task area you wish to allocate them to.  Double-click town center to gather all idle workers.
Blackened figures indicate there are not enough workers to meet optimal production in that task area.
Idle peasants appear in an area if you allocate more than enough labor for the task.
To build a weapon, you must produce or buy the necessary amounts of iron and/or wood.
Use the slider bar to draft peasants from the population into the army.
Don't draft too much of your population or happiness will drop too low.
Choose units by clicking on the appropriate weapon on the wall. You can only raise the types of units you have weapons for.
When your army is ready, click the Create button. Your army appears on the main map when you return to it.
After raising an army, move it toward a neighboring county.
To move an army, click once on it, then click on a destination. The army marches toward the destination until it runs out of moves for the turn.
Right clicking on an army calls up its vital statistics.
To try to conquer a county, attack it by moving your army on top of the town center.
To move your units, click and drag a box around any number of them, then click on a destination.
To attack, select units and then move the cursor onto an enemy unit. When the cursor turns red, click on the unit and your soldiers will attack it.
Get your soldiers inside the castle to fight the defenders. To do this, break through the castle wall or gate with a catapult or battering ram, or go over the castle wall using a siege tower.
Battering rams and siege towers must be moved right up to the castle wall to work. A catapult can attack from a distance.
If the castle has a moat, select some of your soldiers (preferably peasants) and position the cursor over the water.  Click on the water and the soldiers will begin filling in the moat.
Building a castle makes it much harder for enemy troops to conquer your county.
Start with a simple castle design, then upgrade as your materials and builders increase.
You may produce castle-building materials (stone and wood) in your county or buy them from a merchant.
When you give orders to build a castle, some of your laborers in industry will move to castle building until the castle is finished.
If your castle suffers damage from a siege, you may repair it as long as you have the materials and the builders.
When Advanced Farming is on, the number of peasants required for grain farming varies from season to season, and weather and soil fertility affect wheat output.
When Army Foraging is turned on, armies eat food in the county they're traveling in.
When Exploration is turned on, the world outside your county is blacked out. It is gradually revealed as your armies move through and conquer new counties.

Below are a few answers to some of the more commonly asked questions about Lords of the Realm. These replies should allow you to get started in the game
To grow grain, you need 3 things: grain fields, the grain itself, and grain laborers.
To allocate a field to grain growing, click on any non-barren, non-damaged field, and select the grain symbol near the bottom of the panel that appears.
If you have no grain, you must buy some from a merchant when one is in your county.

The computer will automatically plant up to 5 sacks of grain in each field in Winter and allocate the labor needed; less will be planted if you do not have enough grain or labor. Each sack planted will grow into 12 sacks so long as there is enough labor to tend and harvest it during the year.

Grain fields will change in appearance as the seasonal grain cycle progresses. Grain is only planted at the end of the winter turn, and is harvested at the end of the Autumn. You will see the extra grain in your county at the start of each Winter turn.
How do I build a castle?
You may only have one castle in each county.

To build a castle in a county without one, click on the Build Castle button on the control panel. The castle screen displays five castle types. As you click on each castle, the display in the upper right tells you the materials required for that design and how long it will take workers to build it.

In order to build any castle, you must have the stone and wood required for its construction. Click on the thumbs up gauntlet to begin the project. No work will begin until you have all the needed materials. As soon as you have them, the computer will allocate some labor to construct your castle.
To speed up the construction of a castle, assign more workers to the job.
You may follow the same process to upgrade an existing castle.
To make weapons, you need an operational blacksmith, some laborers working there, and the required materials for the weapon you want to make.

To activate a blacksmith, click on it. A weapon icon will appear on your control panel showing the weapon currently being produced. Click on this icon to access the blacksmith shop, where various weapons hang on the walls. To change the weapon being produced, select a hanging weapon.
The panel will show how much wood and iron is needed to produce one unit of the selected weapon. All weapons require some wood, and all but the longbow also require iron.
To get iron or wood, buy them from a merchant or produce them yourself. (Iron production requires an iron mine, and wood production requires a lumber mill.)
To increase production of weapons, allocate more laborers to the blacksmith shop. Make sure you have plenty of materials !.
What should I do each turn?
There is much to be done each turn, depending on your particular strategy. Here are some of your options:
· Adjust your labor allocation to maximize food production, industrial output, and castle construction.
· Check for overcrowding on your cattle fields, and establish more cattle fields (or get rid of cows) if you have overcrowding.
· Visit a merchant, if one is present, and buy cows, grain, weapons, ale, wood, iron, or stone if you need it. Sell extra materials, if you have them, to make some money.
· Adjust your tax rate if it needs adjusting.
· Create an army if one is needed. Move existing armies, and fight battles.
· Transport grain or cows between counties.

You may experience problems running Lords2. If you do, you should exit the game and free up some more memory. (See the readme file for details).

Lords2 is optimised for 256 colour displays. Your windows desktop is not set to this resolution and this may cause problems on some video cards. If problems occur, change your desktop to 256 colours using the display properties box (right click on the desktop and choose settings).

The lords2 display is optimised to use a 640x480 screen area. Your windows desktop is set to 640x480 and this may lead to mouse 'hot spot' problems with the title bar when you switch to full screen mode. If you experience this problem, using the Alt Tab keys will correct it.
